chose: Order the activity newest decided first, by the creation of the record that decided each entry (awards, hugs, received-hugs versions, level ups, drops), keeping Slack's time on every entry and main's entry keys, with one creation-ordered index range per kind and cursors of the form d<decided>_<rank>[_<snapshot>] that still read main's at_rank_created form
over: A changed-since signal on the watched first page that the website would compare; or a stored listing time on late rows
because: #582: a kudos or hug decided late (a directory lookup can recheck for up to 516 minutes) keeps Slack's time and lands below the newest page, the only page the website watches. Decision order makes every new decision land on top, so the existing watch (hasNewActivity) shows it with no website change and after Show new activity the member sees it first; a changed-since signal would need a website change and would still leave the entry deep in the timeline after the reload. New rows only ever land above every cursor, so paging can't repeat or skip; moving received-hugs rows keep their snapshot. Each kind reads one index range instead of up to two, so the page read budget only gains. Entries decided in Slack's order answer as main's (same entries, keys and page sizes); a late entry's day heading can sit above a newer day's.
binding: none: this session owns no active work order
